document.title: Developments in Afghanistan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Unknown] Memo to the State Department Afghanistan Desk showing concern over ISI involvement in the Taliban takeover of Kandahar. A handwritten note says "This AM I've heard that General Babar is running this Taliban op." Babar was the Pashtun Pakistani Interior Minister.

persons.name: Burhanuddin Rabbani
persons.role: Head of the Kabul government; alleged party to a deal with ISI over southern and western Afghanistan

mentions.quote: there is a Rabbani-ISI deal according to which Rabbani has agreed to an ISI move into southern and western Afghanistan

persons.name: Ismail Khan
persons.role: Ruler of Herat; the alleged Rabbani-ISI deal reportedly excluded any challenge to him

mentions.quote: so long as it does not extend to a challenge of Ismail Khan in Herat

persons.name: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar
persons.role: Hezb-i Islami leader, besieging Kabul; ISI reportedly losing faith in him

mentions.quote: the widening gulf between Gulbuddin and ISI -- growing out of ISI's impression that Gulbuddin will be unable to move beyond the Kabul stalemate

persons.name: Mahmoud Mestiri
persons.role: UN special envoy; author of the 'Hesteri plan' for Afghanistan (name garbled in OCR)
persons.status_detail: Identification inferred from the OCR-garbled name 'Hesteri/Hesterd'

mentions.quote: He suspects that the Hesterd plan will either be sabotaged or substantially altered by this undertaking.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Reported as taking over Kandahar and Qalat, possibly moving on Gardez; alleged to be backed by ISI and the Pakistani military.

organizations.name: Inter-Services Intelligence
organizations.notes: Alleged to be deeply involved in the Taliban takeover of Kandahar and Qalat.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Alleged to be seeking to 'pacify' Afghanistan to open a Central Asia-Karachi trade route.

organizations.name: Pakistan Air Force
organizations.notes: Officials allegedly readying Kandahar airport to support larger operations in Helmand and Farah.

organizations.name: Hezb-i Islami (Gulbuddin)
organizations.notes: Gulbuddin's faction, deadlocked at Kabul; relationship with ISI reportedly cooling.

organizations.name: Khalqis
organizations.notes: Former Khalq communists allegedly serving as enforcers in Kandahar.

organizations.name: Afghan Network
organizations.notes: Informal network of Afghan contacts and the diaspora reporting concerns to the author.

events.description: Taliban take over Kandahar and Qalat, allegedly with deep ISI involvement.
Alleged Rabbani-ISI deal permitting an ISI move into southern and western Afghanistan, excluding Ismail Khan's Herat.
Reports that the Pakistan Air Force is readying Kandahar airport to support larger operations in Helmand and Farah.
Rumor that the Taliban may be moving toward Gardez.
Taliban takeover of Kandahar and Qalat, allegedly with ISI involvement.
Alleged Rabbani-ISI deal allowing ISI move into southern/western Afghanistan short of challenging Ismail Khan in Herat.
Reported preparation of Kandahar airport by Pak Air Force for larger operations in Helmand and Farah.
Reported Taliban possible movement toward Gardez.

key_claims: ISI is alleged to be deeply involved in the Taliban takeover of Kandahar and Qalat.
Pakistan may be seeking to pacify Afghanistan to open a Central Asia-Karachi trade route via Herat-Kandahar-Chaman.
A Rabbani-ISI deal reportedly allows an ISI move into the south and west while sparing Ismail Khan's Herat.
ISI is reportedly disenchanted with Gulbuddin's stalemate at Kabul, and Rabbani is exploiting the gulf.
Pakistan Air Force officials are alleged to be readying Kandahar airport for larger operations in Helmand and Farah.
The author warns that Pakistani intervention will generate Afghan resistance, long-term instability and possibly Afghan-Pakistani conflict, and may undermine the UN (Mestiri) plan.
